episodes.186384: A warm front lingered near the Interstate 10 corridor in the afternoon with deep, moist and unsettled SW steering flow aloft. With NE FL within the warm sector, a couple of isolated strong to pulse severe storms and locally heavy rainfall impacted NE FL in the afternoon and early evening with gusty winds and minor wind damage.
episodes.186388: As plentiful moisture and jet energy streamed into the Pacific Northwest, unsettled weather continued across the Sierra and western Nevada. Periods of light showers and stronger westerly winds aloft allowed ridgeline winds to gust to 70 mph through this two day period.  Well not necessarily impactful, travel over the Sierra was difficult at times due to snow levels dropping with a slushy inch or two falling on regional mountain passes.

episodes.186764: A slow moving system brought a training band of thunderstorms with heavy rain to portions of the Florida panhandle, which resulted in some reports of flooding. Rainfall amounts of 5-8 inches were measured.
episodes.187776: During the morning of December 2nd, thunderstorms ignited along a convergent axis parallel to the upper-level flow. This set up over urbanized New Orleans, and caused flash flooding that morning. As that complex moved eastward, a strong cell moved over Lake Pontchartrain and produced a strong wind gust over the southern part of the lake. That cell was the last of the storms that day.

events.narrative: A mesonet station (SCRN2) located 5.5 mi. N of New Washoe City, and mesonet station (AV157) located 2.0 mi WNW of Stead, NV, reported rainfall storm totals of 1.39 inches and 1.01 inches respectively.
Multiple reports of streets flooded across metro New Orleans, with most reports in the Mid City and Uptown areas. A few reports of underpasses closed at Carrolton and Canal.
The Bay County Sheriff's Office reported that 23rd Street near the Golden Corral was becoming impassible due to flash flooding.
